long_biography.plain_text:
An unsigned letter of intent to sell W. M. Jordan to a British buyer reached its Newport News offices during 1984. John R. Lawson II locked it in his desk while completing a rival acquisition plan. Within weeks, he persuaded his father, co-founder Bob Lawson, and partner Nat Macon to match the price and retain local ownership.

As president and chief executive, Lawson guided the business into larger health-care, university, hospitality and research projects across Virginia and the Carolinas. In 2018, he handed the presidency to a successor and assumed the chairmanship, focusing on culture, innovation and property opportunities. His wider legacy includes helping create Virginia Tech's Myers-Lawson School, chairing a billion-dollar university campaign and mentoring a new generation of company leaders.
